document.title: Incident Zero: Build an AI On-Call Engineer
document.event: One-day AI hackathon at PES University
document.theme: Agentic AI for IT Operations: from alert to safe, approved fix

application.name: OpenTelemetry Demo
application.description: An open-source, cloud-native microservices e-commerce application running locally. It emits traces, metrics, and logs, and includes switches for realistic failures.
application.repository_text_visible: GitHub link shown on slide but not fully legible in the photos

document.problem_statement: Build an AI On-Call Engineer that responds to a production incident in a cloud-native application, investigates it using real tools, identifies the root cause with evidence, and resolves it safely with human approval.

solution_workflow.name: Detect the incident
requirements: Receive an alert, such as an error-rate or latency threshold on the demo metrics.

solution_workflow.name: Investigate with tools
requirements: Query traces, metrics, logs, and container health.
Choose the next tool based on findings so far instead of dumping all data into one prompt.

solution_workflow.name: Diagnose with evidence
requirements: Name the failing component and root cause.
Include confidence and exact traces, log lines, or metric values supporting the diagnosis.
Evidence must exist in collected data; invented evidence is penalized.

solution_workflow.name: Propose a safe fix
requirements: Choose only from allowed runbook actions exposed by the Action API.
Give a short reason for the proposed action.
Support dry-run mode and a kill switch.

solution_workflow.name: Ask for human approval
requirements: Show the diagnosis and proposed plan to a human.
Make no changes without explicit approval.

solution_workflow.name: Act and verify
requirements: Execute the approved action through the Action API only.
Check health metrics to confirm recovery.
If recovery fails, roll back and escalate.

solution_workflow.name: Report
requirements: Produce a concise incident report with timeline, root cause, evidence, action taken, and prevention recommendation.

application_faults: Product catalog fails for one specific product
Memory leak in the recommendation service caused by a runaway cache
High CPU or heavy garbage collection in the ad service
infrastructure_faults: A service container is stopped or keeps restarting
Network latency or packet loss between two services
A service is starved of CPU or memory
practice_incident_types_visible.evaluation_note: The slide says ten practice incidents are published at kickoff and final evaluation uses unseen incidents, including infrastructure faults and combinations. The agent must reason from telemetry, not read feature-flag settings.

provided_environment.name: OpenTelemetry Demo
provided_environment.description: Microservices store including frontend, cart, checkout, payment, product catalog, recommendation, ad, shipping, and more; run with Docker Compose and a Locust load generator.

provided_environment.name: Telemetry
provided_environment.description: Traces, metrics, and logs from services through the OpenTelemetry Collector, with bundled trace and metrics viewers.

provided_environment.name: Failure flags
provided_environment.description: Built-in switches for realistic failures, managed by flagd.

provided_environment.name: faultctl
provided_environment.description: Command-line tool to inject a practice incident (a flag or infrastructure fault) and reset everything.

provided_environment.name: Action API
provided_environment.description: Only allowed way for the agent to change the system: restart a service, toggle a feature flag, throttle the load generator, or scale a service (Kubernetes only). Every call is logged.

provided_environment.name: Offline incident bundles
provided_environment.description: Recorded telemetry for each practice incident for laptops that cannot run the full demo.

provided_environment.name: LLM access
provided_environment.description: API key with a spend limit; open-source or local models are also allowed.

provided_environment.name: Template repository
provided_environment.description: Agent skeleton, required output format (JSON schema), README template, and team form.

required_final_deliverables.name: Source code
required_final_deliverables.details: Team repository forked from the template, with a README covering setup, how to run, how the approval gate and kill switch work, and known limitations.

required_final_deliverables.name: Architecture overview
required_final_deliverables.details: One page describing components, tools used by the agent, decision process, and safety controls. A photo of a whiteboard sketch is acceptable.

required_final_deliverables.name: Incident reports
required_final_deliverables.details: Reports produced by the agent for the practice incidents it handled, in the provided JSON schema plus readable form.

required_final_deliverables.name: Evaluation note
required_final_deliverables.details: Which practice incidents the agent got right and wrong in your own testing, and why.

required_final_deliverables.name: Team form
required_final_deliverables.details: Team name, members, who built which part, tools and AI models used (including AI coding assistants), and third-party libraries.

rules: Teams of 5. All code is written on the day, from 09:15; commits before then are not allowed.
Open-source libraries and agent frameworks are allowed. AI coding assistants are allowed if declared in the team form; every member must be able to explain and change the code they submit.
The slide also says: 'All three members must commit code.' This conflicts with the 'Teams of 5' rule; confirm the intended team size with the organizers.
Mentors help teams get unblocked; they do not write code. No outside help.
The agent changes the demo only through the Action API, and only after human approval.
Reading feature-flag settings to diagnose, or tampering with the demo, faultctl, hidden incidents, or scoring harness means disqualification.
Be honest about what does not work. Stating a limitation costs nothing; hiding a failure in the demo loses points.

optional_stretch_goals.name: Incident memory
optional_stretch_goals.description: Reuse earlier incident reports to diagnose a repeat incident faster.

optional_stretch_goals.name: Reviewer agent
optional_stretch_goals.description: A second agent tries to disprove the diagnosis before a human sees it.

optional_stretch_goals.name: Calibrated confidence
optional_stretch_goals.description: Show that stated confidence matches how often the agent is right on the practice set.

optional_stretch_goals.name: Chat-style approval
optional_stretch_goals.description: The on-call human approves or rejects from a simple chat UI or dashboard.

optional_stretch_goals.name: Prevention
optional_stretch_goals.description: After fixing, suggest a code, config, or alerting change that would stop the incident recurring.

incident_id.description: Practice incident identifier supplied by the environment.

reference.description: Trace ID, log reference, metric query, or other retrievable source reference.

action.description: Must be an allowed Action API action.

notes: This JSON is an OCR-based structured extraction of the visible slides, plus a proposed incident-report schema because the organizers' actual JSON schema is not legible/provided in the photos.

Before final submission, replace incident_report_json_schema with the official schema from the template repository if it differs, and populate incident_reports with genuine outputs from your agent. Do not submit fabricated diagnoses or evidence.

The visible slide has a timing discrepancy: the deliverables slide says code freeze at 16:30, while the rules say code is written from 09:15. Treat 16:30 as the stated submission/code-freeze time and confirm details with organizers.
